config.title: Portal

intro.title: Portal
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple portal component that dynamically renders content from one part of your Angular application into another. You will learn the core concept of content projection using Angular's built-in portal and portal outlet features. The main technologies involved are Angular's ComponentFactoryResolver, ViewContainerRef, and the CdkPortal and CdkPortalOutlet directives from the Angular CDK. By the end, you'll understand how to create flexible, reusable UI components that can inject content anywhere in your app's DOM structure.
intro.usecase: Portals in Angular enable developers to render UI components outside their normal DOM hierarchy while maintaining Angular's data binding and lifecycle management. This pattern is essential for creating modal dialogs, tooltips, and notifications that need to appear above other content without CSS positioning hacks. In real applications, portals power dashboard widgets that can be dragged between panels, complex form wizards with floating validation messages, and contextual help panels that overlay specific interface sections. Developers use portals to build maintainable, reusable overlay components that work predictably across different parts of their application.

objectives: Implement a portal host component to define where dynamic content will be rendered.
Configure a portal service to manage the creation and attachment of portal content.
Construct a portal directive to mark template content as a portal source.
Initialize and attach portal content to a designated portal outlet.
Manipulate portal content dynamically by detaching and reattaching it based on user interaction.
Integrate portal functionality into a component to enable dynamic UI updates.
Apply portal concepts to render template content in a different part of the DOM than its declaration.

steps.title: Create the main PortalComponent class with Component decorator
steps.instruction: Define the PortalComponent class with the @Component decorator, including an empty template and selector.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from the imported Angular core APIs to define your component class.

seedCode.App.tsx:
import { Component, ViewContainerRef, TemplateRef, ViewChild, ComponentFactoryResolver } from '@angular/core';

// Define the PortalComponent class with @Component decorator here

steps.expectedOutcome: The PortalComponent class is defined with the @Component decorator, ready for adding portal logic.
successCriteria: PortalComponent class is defined with @Component decorator containing selector and empty template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined the PortalComponent class with the @Component decorator, including selector and template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The PortalComponent class with @Component decorator is not properly defined. Review Angular component structure.

steps.title: Add ViewChild decorator to access the portal outlet container
steps.instruction: Inside the PortalComponent class, add a ViewChild property named 'portalOutlet' that will reference a ViewContainerRef for portal insertion.
steps.hint: Use the @ViewChild decorator with a template reference variable to get access to a ViewContainerRef in your component.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Using ViewChild to get a container reference
@ViewChild('container', { read: ViewContainerRef }) containerRef!: ViewContainerRef;
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a ViewChild property that can access the portal outlet container element.
successCriteria: PortalComponent contains a ViewChild property named 'portalOutlet' that references a ViewContainerRef.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the property is named 'portalOutlet' and uses the ViewChild decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ViewChild property is missing or incorrect. Check that you've added a ViewChild decorator with the correct name.

steps.title: Create a TemplateRef property for the portal content
steps.instruction: Inside the PortalComponent class, add a property named 'portalContent' with the type 'TemplateRef<any>' to hold the content that will be rendered through the portal.
steps.hint: Define a class property with the correct type annotation. You don't need to initialize it yet.
steps.expectedOutcome: The PortalComponent class will have a typed TemplateRef property ready to store portal content.
successCriteria: The PortalComponent class contains a property named 'portalContent' with type 'TemplateRef<any>'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a property named 'portalContent' with the correct type 'TemplateRef<any>' inside the PortalComponent class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The portalContent property is missing or incorrect. It should be a class property with type 'TemplateRef<any>'.

steps.title: Inject ComponentFactoryResolver in the constructor
steps.instruction: Add a constructor to your PortalComponent class that injects ComponentFactoryResolver as a parameter.
steps.hint: Use TypeScript constructor syntax with a private parameter to store the injected service.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: injecting a service
constructor(private myService: MyService) {}
steps.expectedOutcome: The PortalComponent constructor now has ComponentFactoryResolver injected as a dependency, enabling dynamic component creation.
successCriteria: Constructor is added with ComponentFactoryResolver parameter injected and stored as a private property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a constructor, but make sure ComponentFactoryResolver is properly injected as a parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The constructor should inject ComponentFactoryResolver to enable dynamic component creation.

steps.title: Create a method to attach template content to the portal outlet
steps.instruction: Inside the PortalComponent class, create a method named 'attachTemplatePortal' that takes a TemplateRef parameter and uses the portal outlet's ViewContainerRef to create an embedded view.
steps.hint: Use the @ViewChild-decorated property to access the ViewContainerRef, then call its createEmbeddedView() method with the TemplateRef parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a method that can attach template content to the portal outlet when called.
successCriteria: The PortalComponent contains a method named 'attachTemplatePortal' that accepts a TemplateRef parameter and calls createEmbeddedView() on the portal outlet's ViewContainerRef.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the method accepts a TemplateRef parameter and uses createEmbeddedView() on the portal outlet's ViewContainerRef.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method is missing or doesn't properly attach template content. Check that you're using the portal outlet's ViewContainerRef and calling createEmbeddedView() with a TemplateRef parameter.

steps.title: Create a method to clear the portal outlet
steps.instruction: In your PortalComponent class, define a method named clearPortal that calls the clear() method on the portalOutlet ViewContainerRef.
steps.hint: The clear() method on ViewContainerRef removes all views from the container. You can access portalOutlet as this.portalOutlet.
steps.expectedOutcome: A clearPortal method is added to the PortalComponent class that will remove any content from the portal outlet when called.
successCriteria: The PortalComponent has a clearPortal method that calls this.portalOutlet.clear()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your clearPortal method correctly calls the clear() method on the portalOutlet property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The clearPortal method isn't quite right. Remember to define a method that calls clear() on the portalOutlet ViewContainerRef.

steps.title: Add the portal outlet container to the component template
steps.instruction: In the component's template, replace the existing div with a <ng-container> element that has a template reference variable named 'portalOutlet'.
steps.hint: The <ng-container> is a logical container that doesn't add extra DOM elements, making it ideal as a portal anchor point.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: using ng-container as a container
<ng-container #myContainer></ng-container>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now uses <ng-container> with the #portalOutlet reference, providing a clean anchor point for portal content.
successCriteria: The component template contains <ng-container #portalOutlet></ng-container> as the portal outlet.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using <ng-container> with the exact template reference variable name 'portalOutlet'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The portal outlet container wasn't properly added. Remember to use <ng-container #portalOutlet></ng-container> in the template.

steps.title: Add the portal content template to the component template
steps.instruction: Inside the component's template, add a <ng-template> element with a template reference variable named 'portalContent' and some placeholder content (like a heading or paragraph) that will be rendered through the portal.
steps.hint: Place the <ng-template> element after the portal outlet div. Use the #portalContent syntax to create the template reference variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: template with reference variable

This content can be rendered elsewhere
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now contains a <ng-template> element with a template reference variable that can be used as portal content.
successCriteria: The template contains a <ng-template> element with #portalContent reference variable and some content inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a template, but make sure it has the correct reference variable name (#portalContent) and contains some content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the required <ng-template> element with the portalContent reference variable.

steps.title: Add attach and clear buttons to the template
steps.instruction: Add two buttons to the component template: one labeled 'Attach Portal' and one labeled 'Clear Portal'. Place them above the portal outlet div.
steps.hint: Use the <button> element with descriptive text. Place them inside the template string before the existing portal outlet div.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding UI buttons in Angular template
Content area
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains two buttons above the portal outlet, providing UI controls to demonstrate portal functionality.
successCriteria: Two button elements are added to the template with labels 'Attach Portal' and 'Clear Portal', placed before the portal outlet div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added buttons, but make sure you have exactly two buttons with the correct labels ('Attach Portal' and 'Clear Portal') placed above the portal outlet div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the required buttons. Add two <button> elements with the specified labels above the portal outlet div.

steps.title: Wire the attach button to call the attach method
steps.instruction: Add a click event binding to the attach button in your template that calls the attachTemplatePortal method.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (click)="methodName()" on the button element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring a button click to a method
<button (click)="handleClick()">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The attach button will have a click event binding that triggers the attachTemplatePortal method when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element includes (click)="attachTemplatePortal()" event binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the event binding might be incomplete. Make sure you're using Angular's (click) syntax and calling the attachTemplatePortal() method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button doesn't have the correct event binding. Remember to use (click)="attachTemplatePortal()" on the button element.

steps.title: Wire the clear button to call the clear method
steps.instruction: Add a (click) event binding to the clear button in your template that calls the clearPortal method.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (click)="clearPortal()" on the button element.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example: wiring a button to a method -->
<button (click)="handleClear()">Clear</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The clear button will trigger the clearPortal method when clicked, allowing portal content cleanup.
successCriteria: The template contains a button with (click)="clearPortal()" event binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the (click) event binding with the correct method name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The clear button isn't properly wired. Check that you've added (click)="clearPortal()" to the button element.
